source.authors: Caroline M. F. Durif, Daniel Nyqvist, Bastien Taormina, Steven D. Shema, Anne Berit Skiftesvik, Florian Freytet, Howard I. Browman
source.title: Magnetic fields generated by submarine power cables have a negligible effect on the swimming behavior of Atlantic lumpfish (Cyclopterus lumpus) juveniles

value: no effect of the coil-generated magnetic field on activity (time swimming relative to stationary pauses) or distance travelled
method: behavioural: juveniles exposed to an artificial static magnetic field from a coil (on) against coil off (control); activity and distance travelled scored
conditions: Hatchery-reared juveniles (eggs from Skaerneset fisk AS, reared at the Austevoll Research Station), 7 months old, 8 +/- 1 cm; 24 fish per treatment (48 in all). Coil on (static DC field reaching 230 uT, measured along the central axis with a smartphone magnetometer and also estimated by B = 0.2 I/d; the Discussion says up to 220 uT) against coil off as control; each of four raceways (125 x 14 x 7 cm, one fish each, four new fish per trial, filmed 30 min with overhead lights off) sat half inside the coil, so the field formed a gradient from the coil end toward ambient at the outer end, with quadrants A to D (D lowest) defined a posteriori; ambient geomagnetic field 51 uT; treatment (n = 6) and control trials (n = 6) were alternated, not randomised. Swimming speed tested with a linear mixed-effects model (fish as random intercept, likelihood-ratio test), speeds below 0.5 cm/s dropped to remove immobile fish. Speed: chi2(1) = 4.1176, p = 0.042, about 16% slower with the coil on, visible in all quadrants but more pronounced in the middle; speeds from the end quadrants A and D (including the strongest-field end) were removed for edge effect. Activity ratio did not differ between treatments (ANOVA, p = 0.853); total distance did not differ (t-test, df = 46, p = 0.45); the field had no significant effect on where fish spent time along the gradient (Cramer's V = 0.0143).
quote: Juvenile lumpfish activity, defined as the time that the fish spent swimming relative to stationary pauses (attached to the substrate), and the distance travelled, were unaffected by exposure to the artificial MF.
note: Null result for activity and distance travelled. Sentence returned in two abutting pieces by the page tool (said in pieces). Family and order from OBIS (accepted Cyclopterus lumpus (Linnaeus, 1758), Cyclopteridae, Perciformes); not printed on the page. Licence: page prints 'Creative Commons Attribution License'; Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version unspecified. Authors as Crossref (page shows only 'Durif et al.' in the text read). Companion record: swimming speed was reduced. Earlier held in desk-d224 for the quote; the abstract sentence is under 40 words. Statistics and gradient design added from the Results and Methods (audit 330).

method: behavioural: swimming speed (instantaneous speeds) with coil on against coil off, in a raceway

Speed: chi2(1) = 4.1176, p = 0.042, about 16% slower with the coil on, visible in all quadrants but more pronounced in the middle; speeds from the end quadrants A and D (including the strongest-field end) were removed for edge effect. quote: The swimming speed of juvenile lumpfish was reduced (by 16%) when the coil was on indicating that the fish could either sense the MF or the induced electric field created by the movement of the fish through the magnetic field.
note: Sentence returned in three abutting pieces (said in pieces). source.authors: Lei Bian, Xiao Ming Cai, Zong Xiu Luo, Zhao Qun Li, Zong Mao Chen
source.title: Foliage Intensity is an Important Cue of Habitat Location for Empoasca onukii

method: physiological: electroretinogram (ERG) spectral sensitivity of the whole compound eye
conditions: Laboratory-reared adults 2-4 days old from a colony kept at 25 +/- 2 C and 70 +/- 3% RH (not wild-caught). ERG: dark-adapted 30 min, 100 ms monochromatic flashes 5 s apart from a xenon arc lamp through narrow-band filters; maximum quantum flux of each wavelength adjusted to about 10^11 photons cm-2 s-1 and calibrated with neutral-density filters; recorded five times for each sex between 17:00 and 20:00, wavelengths alternating from 300 to 700 nm and then repeated in reverse order (counterbalanced, not randomised), giving ten spectral scans; response amplitudes over a 4-log-unit range converted to equivalent intensities with the Naka-Rushton function and sensitivity taken as the reciprocal; the number of insects is not stated. Sexes did not differ in spectral sensitivity (p > 0.05), so the peaks are pooled. Nonlinear least-squares fitting of three putative visual pigments gave 356, 435 and 542 nm in the amplitude ratio 1:0.6:6.4 (UV:blue:green), a fit not a measured single-cell peak; the next sentence of the paper begins 'It was difficult to perform unicellular recording', so single-cell recordings were not made.
quote: The spectral sensitivity curves of the compound eye have two major peaks, with the primary peak at 540 nm and a secondary peak at 355 nm (Figure 4).
note: Primary ERG peak of the compound eye. Sentence returned in two abutting pieces (said in pieces); the page's trailing '([Figure 4])' is shown as printed. Published as Empoasca onukii; filed under the accepted name Matsumurasca onukii (main's gbif-names.tsv: Empoasca onukii SYNONYM of Matsumurasca onukii; SBDI likewise), audit 330. Family Cicadellidae as printed on the page; order Hemiptera. Licence: page links CC BY 3.0; Crossref CC BY 4.0 vor. ERG peak is a whole-eye sensitivity, not a single pigment lambda max; fitted pigments (356, 435, 542 nm) are in the conditions. new trait: whole_eye_spectral_peak_nm, the key used on main (oa-1 Sympetrum frequens ERG peaks); the fitted pigment maxima stay in conditions.

source.authors: Casper J. van der Kooi, Almut Kelber
source.title: Achromatic Cues Are Important for Flower Visibility to Hawkmoths and Other Insects

method: behavioural: two-choice test between a lighter and a darker blue stimulus of the same hue, exact binomial test against equal choice
value: 11 of 12 responding moths chose the brighter (Light Blue) stimulus first; exact binomial p = 0.006
conditions: Two circular blue flower-like paper stimuli of 2 cm diameter, 'Light Blue' and 'Dark Blue', with the same chromatic properties but different intensities (achromatic), offered together in a flight cage; light level measured at the centre of the cage with a Hagner Screen Master; each newly eclosed, flower-naive moth was tested once and individually on its day of eclosion, in its activity period (first 2 h of night for D. elpenor, daytime for M. stellatarum); a new stimulus array was used for each moth and the left/right position of Light Blue and Dark Blue was randomised; the stimuli were 7 cm apart on a green paper background, which no moth probed; only the first probe was recorded and no reward was given. Pupae were bred on the natural larval food plant (Galium sp.) and eclosed in the flight cage; supplier or laboratory culture is not named. Moths that did not approach and probe the display within 5 min of taking flight were excluded (three D. elpenor and four M. stellatarum), so the counts are of responders. The Methods give no number tested overall. The paper is a Hypothesis and Theory article; the choice experiment is its own, alongside a literature synthesis and optical modelling not used here. Cage illumination (white LEDs reflected from above in an otherwise dark room) adjusted to 10 lux for D. elpenor (about nautical twilight), measured at the cage centre; the two stimuli differ in reflectance under that light. The 12 responders were all that approached; 11 chose Light Blue, 1 Dark Blue.
quote: Of these moths, eleven approached Light Blue first, whereas one chose Dark Blue (p = 0.006, exact binomial test; 99% confidence interval: 0.52–1.00).
note: Sentence returned in two abutting pieces (said in pieces). Family Sphingidae as main's rows for both species (gbif-names.tsv EXACT ACCEPTED), audit 330. Licence: Crossref CC BY 4.0, content-version vor; the page text read had no licence sentence. Issue number not printed in the text read.

method: behavioural: two-choice test between a lighter and a darker blue stimulus of the same hue, exact binomial test against equal choice
value: 21 of 24 moths probed Light Blue (the brighter stimulus); exact binomial p < 0.01
conditions: Two circular blue flower-like paper stimuli of 2 cm diameter, 'Light Blue' and 'Dark Blue', with the same chromatic properties but different intensities (achromatic), offered together in a flight cage; light level measured at the centre of the cage with a Hagner Screen Master; each newly eclosed, flower-naive moth was tested once and individually on its day of eclosion, in its activity period (first 2 h of night for D. elpenor, daytime for M. stellatarum); a new stimulus array was used for each moth and the left/right position of Light Blue and Dark Blue was randomised; the stimuli were 7 cm apart on a green paper background, which no moth probed; only the first probe was recorded and no reward was given. Pupae were bred on the natural larval food plant (Galium sp.) and eclosed in the flight cage; supplier or laboratory culture is not named. Moths that did not approach and probe the display within 5 min of taking flight were excluded (three D. elpenor and four M. stellatarum), so the counts are of responders. The Methods give no number tested overall. The paper is a Hypothesis and Theory article; the choice experiment is its own, alongside a literature synthesis and optical modelling not used here. Cage illumination (white LEDs reflected from above in an otherwise dark room) adjusted to 100 lux for M. stellatarum (about civil twilight), measured at the cage centre; the two stimuli differ in reflectance under that light. The species were tested at different light levels chosen for their activity periods. Of 24, 21 probed Light Blue; the sentence does not state the other 3 chose Dark Blue.
quote: Of 24 M. stellatarum, 21 probed Light Blue (p < 0.01, exact binomial test, confidence interval: 0.61–0.99).
note: Whole sentence returned unbroken. Next sentence of the paper: 'In both species, this indicates a significant preference for the stimulus with higher reflectance and intensity.' Differs from the held chromatic-signal paper (pone.0034629). Family as the Deilephila record. Licence as the Deilephila record.

source.authors: Atsushi Suzuki, Yoichi Sato, Eri Inomata, Yukio Agatsuma, Masakazu N. Aoki, Hikaru Endo
source.title: Light and Substrate Color Preferences in the Marine Isopod Cymodoce japonica
source.journal: Journal of Marine Science and Engineering 14(19): 1858

method: behavioural: time spent in coloured-light compartments (dark, red, green, blue) in paired choice trials
conditions: Two-compartment light choice, one isopod at a time (each experiment conducted 30 times, 30 trials per light pairing), 5 min per trial with presence recorded every minute; the isopod was released at the centre; light from CCS LED panels (ISLM-150X150-BB, -GG, -RR; peak wavelengths blue 470, green 530, red 655 nm; spectra in Supplementary Figure S1, not read) with irradiance at the aquarium bottom set at 15 umol photons m-2 s-1 for each colour (how it was measured is not stated). Animals collected by tweezers from a cultivated Undaria pinnatifida population in Shizugawa Bay, Miyagi Prefecture, in April 2018, held in darkness over 12 h at 15 C and fed U. pinnatifida blades (200 caught; 30 active individuals of 13.0-20.4 mm used; inactive isopods that did not respond to light in preliminary trials were excluded, so results hold for active animals only). Pairings reported: dark v red, dark v green, dark v blue, red v green, red v blue, green v blue. Trial order, compartment side and sex are not reported; at least 1 h dark acclimation before each experiment; GLMM (Poisson, chosen over negative binomial by AIC) with individual as a random factor, which implies the same 30 animals across pairings (not stated outright); light colour tested by likelihood-ratio test. All Results 3.2 pairings: dark v red no difference (p = 0.191); dark longer than green and blue (p < 0.001 each; 19 of 30 moved from dark to green at least once, only 3 from dark to blue); red longer than green and blue (p < 0.001 each); green longer than blue (p < 0.001). Substrate-colour experiment (red, orange, yellow, blue straws) is a separate experiment not used here.
value: no difference in time spent between the dark and red-light compartments (likelihood ratio test, p = 0.191)
quote: There was no significant difference between the time isopods spent in the dark and red-light compartments (Figure 5; likelihood ratio test, p = 0.191).
note: Null result. The authors read it as meaning the isopod 'may either hardly detect red light' (655 nm) or has no preference even if it perceives it (Discussion). Sentence returned in two abutting pieces (said in pieces). Family and order from OBIS (Cymodoce japonica Richardson, 1906, accepted, Sphaeromatidae, Isopoda, taxonID 256965 = WoRMS AphiaID; checked in audit 330); not printed in the passages read.
